title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding transforms categorical variables into a set of binary variables. For the 'sex' column, this means creating two new columns: $$'sex_{male'}$$ and $$'sex_{female'}$$. Each row will have a $$1$$ in one of these columns and a $$0$$ in the other.

title: Properties of the Design Matrix
text: The design matrix \( \Phi_1 \) will have two columns corresponding to $$'sex_{male'}$$ and $$'sex_{female'}$$. Each row will have a $$1$$ in one column and a $$0$$ in the other, ensuring that the sum of each row is $$1$$.

title: Invertibility of a Matrix
text: A matrix is invertible if it is square and has full rank. For \( \Phi_1**T \Phi_1 \) to be invertible, \( \Phi_1 \) must have full column rank.

hintAnswer: Yes, \( \Phi_1 \) has full column rank because the columns are linearly independent.
title: Checking Full Column Rank
text: Does the design matrix \( \Phi_1 \) have full column rank? Consider the columns $$'sex_{male'}$$ and $$'sex_{female'}$$.
choices: Yes, \( \Phi_1 \) has full column rank because the columns are linearly independent.

hintAnswer: \( \Phi_1**T \Phi_1 \) is invertible because \( \Phi_1 \) has full column rank.
title: Conclusion on Invertibility
text: Given that \( \Phi_1 \) has full column rank, what can we conclude about \( \Phi_1**T \Phi_1 \)?
choices: \( \Phi_1**T \Phi_1 \) is invertible because \( \Phi_1 \) has full column rank.
